---
title: "ROS 2 Package Structure"
---

This page describes the minimal layout and boilerplate for a ROS 2 C++ package
that builds correctly under colcon inside the pixi workspace.

---

## Directory layout

```
src/
+-- my_package/
    +-- include/
    |   +-- my_package/
    |       +-- my_node.hpp
    +-- src/
    |   +-- my_node.cpp
    |   +-- main.cpp
    +-- launch/
    |   +-- my_node.launch.py
    +-- CMakeLists.txt
    +-- package.xml
```

Headers live under `include/<package_name>/` so they are importable as
`#include "my_package/my_node.hpp"` from any package that depends on this one.

---

## package.xml

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<?xml-model href="http://download.ros.org/schema/package_format3.xsd"
            schematypens="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"?>
<package format="3">
  <name>my_package</name>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
  <description>My ROS 2 package</description>
  <maintainer email="you@example.com">Your Name</maintainer>
  <license>MIT</license>

  <buildtool_depend>ament_cmake</buildtool_depend>

  <depend>rclcpp</depend>
  <depend>std_msgs</depend>
  <depend>geometry_msgs</depend>
  <depend>px4_msgs</depend>

  <export>
    <build_type>ament_cmake</build_type>
  </export>
</package>
```

Use `<depend>` (not `<build_depend>` + `<exec_depend>`) for libraries that are
needed at both build and runtime — which covers most ROS packages.

---

## CMakeLists.txt

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
project(my_package)

# --- compiler settings ---
if(CMAKE_COMPILER_IS_GNUCXX OR CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang")
  add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic)
endif()

# --- find dependencies ---
find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
find_package(rclcpp REQUIRED)
find_package(std_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(geometry_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(px4_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(Eigen3 REQUIRED)

# --- build target ---
add_executable(my_node
  src/my_node.cpp
  src/main.cpp
)

target_include_directories(my_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
  ${EIGEN3_INCLUDE_DIR}
)

target_compile_features(my_node PUBLIC cxx_std_17)

ament_target_dependencies(my_node
  rclcpp
  std_msgs
  geometry_msgs
  px4_msgs
)

# --- install ---
install(TARGETS my_node DESTINATION lib/${PROJECT_NAME})
install(DIRECTORY launch DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME})

ament_package()
```

::: {.callout-note}
`ament_target_dependencies` handles both include paths and link libraries for
ament packages. Only use `target_link_libraries` for non-ament deps (Eigen,
yaml-cpp, etc.) that expose CMake targets directly.
:::

---

## Node boilerplate (C++)

**`include/my_package/my_node.hpp`**:

```cpp
#pragma once

#include <rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp>
#include <px4_msgs/msg/vehicle_odometry.hpp>

class MyNode : public rclcpp::Node {
public:
    explicit MyNode(const rclcpp::NodeOptions& options = rclcpp::NodeOptions());

private:
    void odometry_callback(const px4_msgs::msg::VehicleOdometry::SharedPtr msg);

    rclcpp::Subscription<px4_msgs::msg::VehicleOdometry>::SharedPtr odom_sub_;
};
```

**`src/my_node.cpp`**:

```cpp
#include "my_package/my_node.hpp"
#include <rclcpp/qos.hpp>

MyNode::MyNode(const rclcpp::NodeOptions& options)
: Node("my_node", options)
{
    /* PX4 topics require BEST_EFFORT QoS — see QoS Profiles page. */
    auto qos = rclcpp::QoS(10).best_effort();

    odom_sub_ = create_subscription<px4_msgs::msg::VehicleOdometry>(
        "/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry", qos,
        [this](const px4_msgs::msg::VehicleOdometry::SharedPtr msg) {
            odometry_callback(msg);
        });
}

void MyNode::odometry_callback(const px4_msgs::msg::VehicleOdometry::SharedPtr msg)
{
    RCLCPP_INFO_THROTTLE(get_logger(), *get_clock(), 1000,
        "pos: [%.2f, %.2f, %.2f]",
        msg->position[0], msg->position[1], msg->position[2]);
}
```

**`src/main.cpp`**:

```cpp
#include <rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp>
#include "my_package/my_node.hpp"

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
    rclcpp::init(argc, argv);
    rclcpp::spin(std::make_shared<MyNode>());
    rclcpp::shutdown();
    return 0;
}
```

---

## Launch file

**`launch/my_node.launch.py`**:

```python
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch_ros.actions import Node


def generate_launch_description():
    return LaunchDescription([
        Node(
            package="my_package",
            executable="my_node",
            name="my_node",
            output="screen",
            parameters=[],
        )
    ])
```

Launch with:

```bash
ros2 launch my_package my_node.launch.py
```

Or via pixi:

```bash
pixi run launch   # if you defined a 'launch' task in pixi.toml
```

---

## Building and running

```bash
# Build the workspace (all packages under src/)
pixi run build

# Run the node directly
pixi run -- ros2 run my_package my_node

# Or via launch file
pixi run -- ros2 launch my_package my_node.launch.py
```

After editing source files, re-run `pixi run build`. With `--symlink-install`
(default in the build task), Python and resource files are symlinked so they
update without a rebuild — C++ sources still require a rebuild.

---

## Adding a new package

1. Create the directory under `src/`:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p src/my_new_package/{include/my_new_package,src,launch}
   ```
2. Write `package.xml` and `CMakeLists.txt` as shown above.
3. Run `pixi run build` — colcon discovers the new package automatically.

No registration in `pixi.toml` is needed. colcon scans `src/` recursively for
`package.xml` files.
